strongest_results.name: fixed log-squared complete-period theorem
strongest_results.statement: For H=floor((log X)^2), a=C log X/(H L), and q=floor(log_3 X), the complete-CRT good-class density is at most X^{-C log_3 X(1-o(1))}, while the relative nonzero Fourier energy of W^q is O((log_3 X)^2/log_2 X)=o(1).

strongest_results.name: moving low-conductor interval transfer
strongest_results.statement: For Phi=log X log_3 X/log_2 X, the explicit cutoff D=X exp(-2 Phi) gives sum_I W_{<=D}=N mu(1+O(exp(-Phi))). In particular every fixed conductor range D=X^kappa, kappa<1, transfers with relative error X^{-1+kappa+o(1)}.

strongest_results.name: subpower stopping frontier and exact suffix conditioning
strongest_results.statement: The normalized absolute crossing-frontier mass through X^kappa z is exp(O(log X log_3 X/log_2 X))=X^{o(1)}. Conditioning modulo a crossing conductor maps the suffix exactly to another H-forbidden-residue weight on an interval of length N/c.

strongest_results.name: uniform suffix black-box counterexample
strongest_results.statement: A suffix theorem uniform over every start and arbitrary forbidden sets is impossible: CRT gives an all-inactive class of weight one, forcing A(M)>=(M mu_suffix)^{-1}. A viable continuation must retain the inherited start phase and its correlation with the crossing residue.

exact_route_barriers: Blockwise polynomial-modulus transfer followed only by scalar generalized Holder retains o(log X) zero-mode exponent.
Any low-conductor sum-of-squares majorant with square conductor at most X^kappa has mean at least X^{-kappa}, far above the required X^{-C+o(1)}.
The canonical soft Selberg denominator at every fixed polynomial level has log mass o(q log X), exponentially below the qC log X complete-period target.
The fully uniform transformed-suffix interval theorem suggested by a crude stopping recurrence is false by an all-inactive CRT class.
remaining_gap: Prove a one-sided signed high-conductor tail, equivalently a phase-sensitive bound for inherited frontier-suffix correlations. The state must retain interval length, suffix prime endpoint, and inherited starting phase; taking a supremum over arbitrary suffix intervals destroys the needed information.
